div.p:
Giorgio Joyce al Sig.
Esra Ezra Pound.

p.foreign: Ostia! Chi me dize qualcosa, arra? Ghe pianto un pugno entel muso, cossa?

div.note: This card is inscribed to Pound by JJ’s son Giorgio (1905-1976), and bears a humorous text written and initialed by JJ. The other side shows a photo of Giorgio, aged 14 or close to 15, standing in a serious, formal pose and wearing a suit and tie. This is most likely the photograph that JJ planned to send in his letter to Pound of 5 June 1920 but could not locate and said he would send later, possibly in the “next post” (JJ to Pound, 5 June 1920). In that same letter he said that Giorgio “eats about four times as much [as I] and dresses much better.” By age 15, Giorgio was a handsome, athletic youngster, over six feet tall, who had already shown ability as a distance swimmer (Ellmann, JJ 434, 485). The card was not mailed as a postcard, so it was either enclosed with another letter or, more likely, delivered by hand when JJ and Giorgio visited the Pounds in Sirmione in June 1920.

note.p: In Triestine dialect, this text reads, roughly: “Christ! Look, who’s telling me something? What? I’ll punch him in the mug.” “Ostia” is a profane use of a word meaning host or communion wafer. The word “ara,” or, as JJ tended to spell it, “arra,” means “look” but in Triestine is used as an emotional intensifier (see John McCourt, The Years of Bloom: James Joyce in Trieste 1904-1920 [Madison: University of Wisconsin Press, 2000], 54-55). JJ’s misspelling of a number of words (“dize” for “disi”; “arra” for “ara”; “entel” for “intel”; “cossa” for “cosa”) may be due to the fact that he learned only spoken Triestine and probably wrote down words as he heard them. (Thanks to Giovanna Vincenti, Fulvio Rogantin, and Elisa Susmel for transcription explanation, and translation of this text.)

The text, both its words and spirit, might be rendered in the abusive vernacular used by Privates Carr and Compton, the drunken British soldiers who threaten and assault Stephen Dedalus at the end of the “Circe” episode of Ulysses, on which JJ was working at this time: “So help me fucking Christ! What’s that you’re saying, eh? I’ll biff him one in the eye, get me?” (For the ingredients of this translation, see U 15.4370-4797.) JJ seems to have written the little Triestine speech as a bit of dialogue attributed to the Giorgio of the photograph, whose tall form and stern expression could easily suggest a young man squaring off for a round of fisticuffs.
